title: Turn-level micro-interactions — fieldnotes
content:
Context:
This is a very small personal notebook for 1:1 experiments around 'turn-level' UX and economics. Not a formal PRD — more a stitched-together set of hypotheses, tiny flows, and experiment ideas. Aim: reduce per-conversation token cost while keeping perceived fluidity and utility for power users.

Why micro-interactions instead of session-level changes:
- Many apps pay per-turn; small UX changes can measurably cut tokens without heavy infra work.
- Easier to A/B, roll back, and instrument compared to model changes.
- Can be implemented client-side or with simple routing rules (no new model variants).

High-level hypothesis:
- If we provide a set of composable interaction primitives (short explicit system prompts, optional summary/compaction toggles, configurable reply-length caps, and token-aware hints), product teams can lower average tokens/turn by 20–40% on certain workflows while user satisfaction drops <5%.

Key assumptions (to validate):
1) Users prefer slightly abbreviated replies vs. increased latency from extra network hops.
2) Context-preserving compression (prefix summarization) is less harmful than naive truncation for task-oriented dialogs.
3) Low-cost signals (touchtime, user role, message length) are sufficient to pick a conservative micro-optimization policy per-turn.

Proposed primitives (name + quick intention + implementation notes):
A) LightTrim (brief reply hint) — one-token flag in metadata that sets max_tokens ~ 0.6x typical.
   - Intention: force concise answers for status updates and confirmations.
   - Impl: client attaches meta: {micro_mode: "lighttrim"}; server enforces soft cap.
B) AnchorSumm (inline micro-summary) — prefix a machine-generated 1–2 sent summary of last N turns (KV cache-friendly).
   - Intention: allow context compression at the boundary of long threads.
   - Impl: call cheap summarizer model or use cached summary; include as system content instead of raw history.
C) PromptKick (signal-driven system prompt injection) — small template inserted when the user intent is known (e.g., "summarize", "ticket update").
   - Intention: guide output shape and length without changing model.
D) GateResponse (interactive 'more' affordance) — return a concise answer and provide a continuation token the client can fetch for the full expansion.
   - Intention: reduce waste when users accept short answers 80% of the time.
   - Impl: support streaming + truncated final token plus continuation handle.
E) EchoLimit (smart echo avoidance) — detect paraphrased user text and avoid re-stating it verbatim; replace with "acknowledged" placeholders or metadata.

Example flows / user stories:
- US1: As a project manager, I want short daily standup summaries so I can skim quickly. (LightTrim + AnchorSumm)
  Acceptance: Average tokens per PM user drop 35% during AM window; no more than 3% drop in NPS for that cohort.
- US2: As a helpdesk agent, I want an initial short triage reply and an option to expand, so I can triage faster. (GateResponse + PromptKick)
  Acceptance: First-contact resolution time improves or remains same; click-to-expand < 20% per session.
- US3: As a developer using the API, I want a continuation handle so I can fetch long outputs only when necessary. (GateResponse API ergonomics)
  Acceptance: Implementation adds <= 2 server calls for full expand; average tokens saved per request measurable in billing logs.

Metrics / signals to track (what to collect first):
- tokens_in, tokens_out, tokens_saved_by_primitive (tag requests with primitive id)
- click_expand_rate for GateResponse
- median latency per primitive (ensure we don’t add > 50ms p95)
- downstream satisfaction proxy: short survey or rate (thumbs) or ephemeral NPS for exposed cohort
- error / fallback rate when AnchorSumm fails or produces hallucinated context

Experiment plan (quick iteration loop):
1) Build client flagging + server-side tag to apply LightTrim and GateResponse on small % of traffic (start 1%).
2) Run 2-week collection: measure tokens/out, expand clicks, latency.
3) Implement AnchorSumm as a separate cheap summarizer pipeline (use micro model or heuristic) and pilot on threads > 8 turns.
4) Combine primitives in factorial A/B for selected flows (standup bot, helpdesk).

Implementation considerations and constraints:
- Billing: need mapping from primitive->billing attribution so customers can see savings. Add tag in usage logs.
- Security: AnchorSumm may summarize PII; ensure any summarizer runs under same data handling controls as model runs and redaction hooks active.
- Compatibility: GateResponse handles streaming + continuation IDs; make sure SDKs expose convenience helpers.
- Monitoring: add regression alerts for QA signals (satisfaction drop, hallucination spikes).

Quick mock of an API call (pseudo):
POST /v1/responses
{
  "model": "rwd-std-1",
  "input": "What's the status on project X?",
  "meta": {"micro_primitive": "lighttrim"}
}
Response: concise text with tokens_used hint and primitive_id

Open questions / unknowns (TODO):
- How often will users click expand? If expand rate > 30% then GateResponse loses value. Need baseline.
- Can we get away with a cheap summarizer that doesn't regress on facts? Fallback policy required.
- UX wording: how to signal truncation without alarming users about losing content? ("Short answer — click to expand")
- Admin controls: should org admins be able to disable certain primitives? (probably yes for compliance)

Next actions (small next-steps):
- [ ] Instrument a token-tagging field on response logs (LR-4821) — owner: engineering, estimate 2d
- [ ] Prototype LightTrim in SDKs (js + py) — owner: devex, estimate 1d
- [ ] Run a 1-week internal dogfood on PM standup bot (Ava) — collect click rates and token counts
- [ ] Draft small product note for CD/ops with control flags and admin toggles

Notes to self / random thoughts:
- Might combine EchoLimit with LightTrim for message types that are confirmation-heavy (e.g., "Got it, will do X")
- GateResponse continuation handles could be cheap signed URLs returning tokens for a short TTL to avoid state explosion
- Consider a "conservative" preset that only applies LightTrim to messages under 200 chars to reduce user surprise

References:
- Look at LR-3820 for previous continuation work (remind: fetch thread)
- Slack thread: #product-microux has customer anecdotes about preferring short answers for search-like queries

Bottom line: Small, per-turn UX levers feel like low-friction wins for cost-conscious customers. Need to validate expand-click behavior and summarizer fidelity before broad rollout.

(End of notes)
